title: Marriage, Past the Tips
subtitle: For a marriage that needs more than technique — four essays, a study, and a book.
forWhom: For two people who are not in crisis and not fine either, and who suspect the slow drift is more dangerous than the loud fight.

movements.heading: Read these first
movements.note: Start with the quiet erosions nobody warns you about — the drift, the silence, and the vow you did not understand when you made it.

items.label: The Vow You Didn't Understand When You Made It
items.blurb: You promised something in your twenties that only your fifties can explain. Covenant, not contract.

items.label: The Slow Drift That Ends More Marriages Than Affairs Do
items.blurb: Most marriages do not blow up. They cool, one unremarkable evening at a time.

items.label: What Silence Actually Costs a Marriage
items.blurb: The conversation you kept avoiding is still happening — in the distance between you.

items.label: What the Bible Really Says About Submission in Marriage
items.blurb: The most abused word in the wedding canon, read in the context its abusers skip.

movements.heading: Then work the study
movements.note: Covenant is a five-session study of marriage as covenant rather than contract — conflict, forgiveness, and the gospel shape of staying. Written from inside a marriage, not above one.

items.label: Covenant — a study on marriage
items.blurb: Five sessions for married couples, engaged pairs, or a group of both.

movements.heading: Then read the book, free
movements.note: Marriage: Covenant & Roles collects the essays on what marriage actually is and how two people lead and serve each other. Read the whole thing here.

items.label: Marriage: Covenant & Roles — read free
items.blurb: Seven chapters on one flesh, headship and submission read honestly, and the long work of staying.

items.label: Find James's books in the bookstore
items.blurb: Print and ebook editions of the full library.
